SELECTED_INDEX: 9
CONFIDENCE: 0.21
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows only alkyl-type C–H stretches (strong bands at 2879, 2908 and 2964 cm⁻¹) plus typical CH₂ / CH₃ deformations at 1466 and 1450 cm⁻¹, with no bands for C=C, C≡C or carbonyl groups.  A pronounced Raman band at 835 cm⁻¹ together with another at 960 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of cyclohexane-type ring-breathing / C–C stretching modes, which are absent in acyclic alkanes but appear in substituted cyclohexanols.  Among the candidates, only #8 and #9 contain a cyclohexane ring; #9 (CC1CC(C)CC(O)C1) is a secondary cyclohexanol with several CH₂ groups, consistent with the strong 2879/2908 cm⁻¹ pair and moderate 2964 cm⁻¹ (fewer CH₃ groups than #8, which carries a tert-butyl substituent that would enhance the 2960 cm⁻¹ CH₃ band).  Therefore candidate 9 best matches the observed Raman features.
